title: Enterprise 251-user billing walkthrough
summary: A 13-step guided walkthrough of included pools, paid overage, budget precedence, attribution, exclusions, policy blocking, and monthly reset in a 251-seat synthetic enterprise.

steps.title: Steady multi-org consumption
steps.description: Inspect 646,500 seeded credits distributed deterministically across all 251 users and 10 organizations.
steps.expected: All seeded usage is accepted from included credits, every metered budget remains at $0, and 12,400 enterprise credits remain.

steps.title: Pool exhaustion and first paid overage
steps.description: An individual-budget user submits a 20,000-credit burst after accepted seed usage has left 12,400 enterprise credits.
steps.expected: The event splits into 12,400 included and 7,600 metered credits for exactly $76.00.

steps.title: Threshold alerts at 75, 90, and 100
steps.description: A transformation-program user adds 2,000 metered credits.
steps.expected: The user budget raises 75%, the enterprise budget raises 90%, and the cost-center budget raises 100%, with the documented reliability strings.

steps.title: Duplicate-threshold suppression
steps.description: The same user adds 500 credits while remaining above 75% but below 90%.
steps.expected: Usage is accepted and the previously triggered 75% user alert does not fire again.

steps.title: Soft organization-budget breach
steps.description: An unattributed vendor consumes 1,500 metered credits.
steps.expected: The organization budget reaches 125%, alerts fire, usage stays accepted, and no cost-center metered budget changes.

steps.title: Hard-stop rejection
steps.description: A controlled-program user attempts 1,500 metered credits against a $10 hard budget.
steps.expected: The event is blocked atomically and pool plus budget state remain identical to the previous step.

steps.title: User budget spans an included-pool boundary
steps.description: Inspect the earlier 20,000-credit burst after the shared-pool boundary.
steps.expected: The individual ULB grew by the full $200 event value while metered budgets grew only by the $76 overage.

steps.title: User-budget precedence
steps.description: A universal-only user consumes 1,000 credits after individual and cost-center cases have already run.
steps.expected: The new event moves only the universal ULB; cumulative results show individual, then cost-center, then universal precedence.

steps.title: Direct cost-center assignment wins
steps.description: A Product Delivery user directly assigned to the product programme consumes 1,000 credits.
steps.expected: The product-programme budget moves and the organization-mapped Central IT budget does not.

steps.title: Cost-center exclusion
steps.description: An unassigned-seat leaver in the excluded transformation programme consumes 1,000 credits before cycle end.
steps.expected: The event is accepted and moves the excluded cost-center budget but not the enterprise budget, contrasting with the normal programme event.

steps.title: Disable paid AI usage
steps.description: The enterprise disables paid AI usage after September pools are exhausted.
steps.expected: Configuration changes without retroactively changing earlier accepted overage.

steps.title: Paid-usage policy blocks overage
steps.description: A universal-budget user attempts another 1,000 credits while metered budgets still have headroom.
steps.expected: The event is blocked because paid usage is disabled, and counters remain atomic.

steps.title: Seat lifecycle and month-end reset
steps.description: On October 1, the prior transformation user consumes 4,581 credits in the new cycle.
steps.expected: The October pool and budget state keys reset, September history remains, and the 75% user threshold can fire again; fixture lifecycle users retain the documented proration, unassignment, and revoke semantics.
